list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: A mononuclear Ce(IV) centre is bound to four bis(dimethylsilyl)amido nitrogen atoms in a distorted tetrahedral geometry; Si–H groups make secondary agostic contacts. No THF is bound in the crystal structure.

synthesis.procedure: A solution of precursor 1 in THF was added in one portion to PhICl2 in THF in the dark. The immediately red solution was stirred for 1 h, then the volatiles were removed under vacuum. Alternative preparations used trityl chloride or hexachloroethane with 1 in toluene.
synthesis.temperature: ambient temperature for reaction; −35 °C for crystallization (−40 °C in alternative preparations)
synthesis.time: 1 h (PhICl2 route); 0.5 h (trityl chloride route); 18 h (hexachloroethane route)
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: After vacuum removal of volatiles, hexane (2 mL) was added and the mixture cooled to −35 °C to obtain dark-red X-ray-quality crystals. Alternative preparations crystallized from concentrated toluene at −40 °C.
synthesis.yield: 20% crystallized (PhICl2 route); 60% by NMR (trityl chloride route); 0.116 g, 0.17 mmol, 45% crystallized (hexachloroethane route)

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: A discrete pentanuclear Ce(III) cluster in which each Ce centre is six-coordinate and approximately distorted octahedral. Terminal and μ2-bridging bis(dimethylsilyl)amido ligands accompany μ2-, μ3-, and μ4-chloride bridges; the molecule has a twofold axis along Ce(1)–Cl(4). Si–H groups of the bridging amides make agostic contacts.

synthesis.procedure: A toluene solution of donor-free precursor 1a was added in one portion to a toluene solution of PhICl2 in the dark. The solution immediately changed from yellow to red and was stirred for 1 h. Volatiles were removed under vacuum before crystallization.
synthesis.temperature: ambient temperature for reaction; −35 °C for crystallization
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: After removal of volatiles under vacuum, hexane (2 mL) was added to the oily residue and the mixture cooled to −35 °C, producing colourless X-ray-quality crystals.
